posts.author: first_gen_saver
posts.title: FCNR deposits at 5.1% — am I missing a catch vs T-bills?
posts.body: Bank is pitching 5.1% on a 2-year FCNR. T-bills pay similar with zero India paperwork. What actually breaks the tie for an NRI on H-1B?
posts.bodyFull:
Bank is pitching 5.1% on a 2-year FCNR. T-bills pay similar with zero India paperwork. What actually breaks the tie for an NRI on H-1B?

I've read the brochure version — tax-free in India, repatriable — but I want the catches from people who actually held one to maturity.

comments.author: dallas_desi
comments.text: Held two to maturity. The paperwork is fine — the catch is breaking one early: you forfeit most interest.

comments.author: priya_taxes
comments.text: Three real catches: (1) premature withdrawal usually forfeits interest below 1 year; (2) FCNR interest is India-tax-free but US-taxable — it lands on your 1040 and needs FBAR over $10k; (3) repatriation is clean only from the FCNR — once in NRO, you're in TDS territory. If you'll be US-resident both years, T-bills win on simplicity.

comments.author: first_gen_saver
comments.text: This is exactly what the brochure never says. Thank you 🙏

posts.title: REIT index vs the Gurgaon flat: I ran 15 years of numbers
posts.body: Rent yields, vacancy, INR depreciation, the works. The flat wins only if you assume 9% appreciation forever. Spreadsheet in comments.
posts.bodyFull:
Rent yields, vacancy, INR depreciation, the works. The flat wins only if you assume 9% appreciation forever. Spreadsheet in comments.

Biggest surprise: maintenance + society fees ate 22% of gross rent over the period. Nobody prices that in when uncle says 'property never loses'.

comments.author: dallas_desi
comments.text: The INR depreciation line is the one people refuse to look at. Great work.

posts.title: INFY ADR vs holding in India — dividend tax treatment surprised me
posts.body: The ADR route sidesteps the 20% India withholding headache on my US return. Am I reading the DTAA right?
posts.bodyFull:
The ADR route sidesteps the 20% India withholding headache on my US return. Am I reading the DTAA right?

Context: long INFY either way, just optimizing where it sits.

comments.author: priya_taxes
comments.text: Broadly yes — ADR dividends come through the US custodian with treaty rates applied. Keep the 1042-S if any withholding shows up; the foreign tax credit math is cleaner.
